pr_title: sql: add readable_high_water_timestamp column to SHOW CHANGEFEED JOBS
pr_body:
Epic: CRDB-39390

Fixes: #132278

Release note (sql change): Adds column "readable_high_water_timestamp"
to the output of SHOW CHANGEFEED JOBS. "high_water_timestamp" still
exists and is in epoch nanoseconds. This human readable form will be
easier to consume.

re: the test failure, I have two thoughts on why this might have happened, and maybe others can check on my theories. You can try stress testing this and see if you can repro by `./dev test pkg/ccl/changefeedccl -f TestShowChangefeedJobsShowsHighWaterTimestamp --stress`. 

1. This is truncating precision somehow different from `hlc_to_timestamp`.
```
highWaterTimestamp := time.Unix(0, int64(highWaterHLC.Float64)).UTC()
```

<del> 
2. I wonder if it is possible that the data in the table is updated after `high_water_timestamp` is processed but before `hlc_to_timestamp(high_water_timestamp)` is fetched. You might need something like the following to capture the data to be consistent. But I'm not entirely sure whether this is possible here. I guess it depends on your transaction isolation level?

```
WITH data AS (
    SELECT high_water_timestamp FROM table t
)
SELECT hlc_to_timestamp(high_water_timestamp), high_water_timestamp FROM data;
```
</del> 

Update: this is not possible given it is executed inside one transaction

issue_context.title: cdc: add human readable high water timestamp to show changefeed jobs
issue_context.body:
`SHOW CHANGEFEED JOBS` includes the high water mark timestamp (the timestamp of the last checkpoint) in epoch nanoseconds. It would be useful to also have this in human-readable form in an additional column for easier consumption.

Jira issue: CRDB-42914

Epic CRDB-39390
